Apple trees grown from seed rarely produce fruit identical to the parent — most orchards use grafted trees instead.
Apple trees typically take 2–4 years after planting before they bear fruit.
Cross-pollination between different apple varieties usually produces better fruit yields.
Most apple varieties need 500–1,000 chill hours below 7°C each winter to bloom properly.

Apple scab thrives in cool, wet spring weather — good air circulation reduces risk.
Cedar apple rust requires two host plants, apple and juniper or cedar trees, to complete its life cycle.
